name: Function Calling
tools: OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs

beginner.summary: For developers who can write Python or JavaScript and call REST APIs but have never wired a language model to their own code. Covers what a function call really is (the model emits a name and JSON arguments, your code runs them), JSON Schema parameter definitions, naming and descriptions, reading and parsing responses, argument validation, returning results, tool_choice modes, parallel calls, error results, message history rules, first calls on Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock Converse and Ollama, schema-constrained output, logging and a tested single-turn client capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working Python 3.11+ or Node.js 20+ code and calls an HTTP API with curl or a client library
Reads and writes JSON and knows the difference between a JSON string and a parsed object
Has an API key (or credits) for at least one hosted model provider, or a laptop able to run Ollama with a small model
outcomes: Define functions with correct JSON Schema and descriptions, and explain what the model returns and what your code must do next
Run a complete request, execute, result, final-answer loop on OpenAI, then repeat it on Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock Converse or Ollama
Validate every argument set with jsonschema or Pydantic, return errors and empty results in the shape each provider expects, and keep message history valid
Ship a tested single-turn client that logs every call and measures selection accuracy against a labelled prompt set

intermediate.summary: For developers who have built a basic call-and-result loop and now need production-grade behavior. Covers strict mode and structured outputs, schema patterns with unions and recursion, coercion and semantic validation, repair loops, multi-turn and dependent calls, streaming on OpenAI, Anthropic and Bedrock, reasoning-model state, a provider adapter layer, document and image data extraction, wrapping REST APIs from OpenAPI, rate limits and idempotency, concurrent fan-out, large results, and offline testing.
prerequisites: Has completed a working call, execute, result loop on at least one provider and validates arguments with Pydantic or jsonschema
Writes asynchronous Python (asyncio, httpx) or equivalent async JavaScript
Has API access to OpenAI plus one of Anthropic, Gemini or Bedrock, and can run pytest in a CI-style environment
outcomes: Design strict-mode schemas with unions, nested objects and nullable fields, and drive schema violations to zero
Implement multi-turn loops with iteration caps, dependent calls, repair loops and streaming accumulators on three providers
Build a provider adapter and extraction pipelines that turn documents and images into validated records with measured field accuracy
Orchestrate REST APIs with retries, idempotency keys, concurrency limits and pagination, and test everything offline with recorded fixtures

advanced.summary: For engineers who run function calling in production or plan to. Covers accuracy measurement (metrics, Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard, custom harnesses with regression gates), prompt and schema experiments, cost modeling, prompt caching, latency engineering, large catalogs, constrained decoding internals, open-weight serving with vLLM and Ollama, fine-tuning data, provider-specific behavior on Gemini, Bedrock, Anthropic and OpenAI, failure taxonomies, argument hardening, batch workloads, and operations with fallbacks and migrations.
prerequisites: Has built a multi-provider function calling client with strict schemas, streaming and offline tests
Comfortable with statistics basics: proportions, confidence intervals and significance tests
Has access to a GPU or a hosted endpoint for an open-weight model, plus API keys for at least two hosted providers
outcomes: Measure selection, argument and abstention accuracy with confidence intervals, run BFCL and gate releases on regression tests
Model and cut cost and latency using prompt caching, fewer round trips, concurrency and catalog retrieval
Serve open-weight models with vLLM or Ollama, explain chat templates and parsers, and prepare fine-tuning data for calls
Operate function calling in production with failure taxonomies, argument hardening, batch jobs, fallbacks and canary model migrations
